## F2 — how a click reaches the sample
Put to him as an engine behaviour change for every Dioxus native app with a custom widget, with the measurement (two
driver clicks accepted, the widget hears both, the app counts 0 clicks and 0 double clicks; the engine hands a pointer
event on a canvas to the widget and returns before it makes the click, `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs:183-207`)
and option A's cost: one function in blitz-dom, one engine check in both layout modes, the phase's row read re-run.

Options as put: A the engine still makes the click (marked recommended) · B a `div` over the canvas catches the
clicks · C the widget owns the input.

His answer: «A: движок создаёт click (Recommended)»

The forks file's option **A**: after handing the event to the widget the engine runs the click and double-click
synthesis for a canvas too, so the app's `onclick` and `ondoubleclick` on the canvas fire; the widget still hears every
event.

## F1 — is Circle Drawer served by `escher-session` in this chunk
Options as put: A not now (marked recommended) · B serve it now (40 hits in 15 files of served-list sites, 30 count
phrases, new cross-OS rows, the provider leg a boundary widening; the entry splits).

His answer: «A: не сейчас (Recommended)»

The forks file's option **A**: an in-process stand boot read by its checks; no carrier, count or served list moves; it
is served at «Cold-agent bar» (v040-15).

Shown to him as the escher overseer's technical answers, told so he could overturn them:
- F3 option A: the canvas paints each circle's diameter at its centre (numbers only);
- F4 option A: a driver click lands at the canvas's centre only — no offset argument on `click` now; a stated limit

- F5 option A: the canvas states itself as `role="group"` named «Drawing area»;
- the circle list reaches the widget as one `data-circles` attribute.

His answer: «Оставить как решил escher-overseer (Recommended)»

He overturned none. In the records these four stay the escher overseer's word — a delegate's — and go to his batch at
the epoch boundary; they are not his own rulings.

## Epoch 3's boundary (not this chunk's plan)

off to Epoch 4's boundary. It was not the option the dialog recommended.

title: The F2 A mechanism, read at HEAD `a199c213e`

data.head: ## The F2 A mechanism, read at HEAD `a199c213e`

body:
- `handle_dom_event` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs:118`) runs an event's default action after the app's
  listener chain. A `default_prevented` event first runs `record_pointerdown` / `handle_pointerup` (`:136-140`) and
  returns. Otherwise a custom-widget target (`:183-207`, behind `custom-widget`) maps the event to a `UiEvent`, hands
  it to `Widget::handle_event`, sets focus on a pointer down or up, and `return`s before the default-action `match`
  (`:209`).

- So for a widget target, three engine steps never run: `record_pointerdown` (`events/pointer.rs:383`), which counts
  the click (`doc.click_count`, 500 ms and 2 px on the document's clock); `handle_pointerup` (`:744`), which queues
  the UA `Click` (`:791`); and `handle_click` (`:800`), which queues `DoubleClick` when `click_count == 2` (`:812-813`).

- A queued UA event runs the app's listener chain first (Dioxus dispatch through `data-dioxus-id`), then
  `handle_dom_event` again. A `Click` on a widget maps to no `UiEvent` (`events/mod.rs:105`), so the widget arm
  returns for it too. The equality F2 A needs: for a custom-widget target, a pointer down then up at one point
  queues one `Click` to the target, and a second pair within 500 ms and 2 px also queues one `DoubleClick`. Under it,
  the app's `onclick` and `ondoubleclick` on the `<object>` fire through the ordinary listener chain, and the widget
  still hears every pointer event first.

- `handle_click`'s walk is not wanted for a widget: `click_walk` matches no element arm for an `<object>`, and
  `handle_click` then calls `doc.clear_focus()` (`:805-807`), undoing the focus the widget arm set. So the widget's
  `Click` default action queues `DoubleClick` alone and runs no walk.

- `handle_dom_event` is upstream's function. Escher's addition goes into a function of its own, one call in
  upstream's body (arch · stack-and-technologies/decision/fork-additions-in-own-functions).

- No existing test asserts a widget target gets no click: `git grep -n -l 'CustomWidgetAttr\|custom_widget' -- tests`

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas · **Version:** escher-0.4.0

The stand's Circle Drawer moves its drawing area onto a real canvas: an `<object>` carrying a widget painted from Rust
(architecture · established-decisions/decision/custom-widget-object). The widget paints the app's circles and each
circle's diameter as text shaped from the document's own fonts (architecture · standard-contracts/contract/nodes-widgets/widget-fonts),
so on the stand the text comes from the bundled DejaVu Sans (architecture · standard-contracts/decision/stand-typography-dejavu-sans).
Measured on the stand in process, in both layout modes. The canvas's element shot joins the cross-OS digest table (test-plan ·
test-strategy/decision/canvas-shots-cross-os-by-digest). That completes matrix#v040-09.
The forks are answered (`inputs#I2`, relayed verbatim; the resume on them the operator's, `inputs#I3`):

- **F2 A, the founder's ruling — the engine still makes the click.** Measured at P3, an app's `onclick` and
  `ondoubleclick` on a canvas `<object>` never fire: the widget arm of `handle_dom_event` hands a pointer event to the
  widget and returns before the engine counts the click, queues `Click`, or queues `DoubleClick` (research §The F2 A
  mechanism; `evidence/probe-cd-click.log`, `clicks 0 dbl 0`). After the chunk, a custom-widget target still gets
  that synthesis after the widget has the event, so the app's handlers on the canvas fire and the widget still hears
  every pointer event. It is an engine change for every document behind `custom-widget`, so for every Dioxus native
  app. It is flagged upstreamable, nothing is sent (architecture ·
  established-decisions/decision/direct-engine-changes-flagged-upstreamable), and it sits in an escher function with
  one call in upstream's body (architecture · stack-and-technologies/decision/fork-additions-in-own-functions).
  Precedent: a cancelled pointerup still clicks (security-plan · input-validation/decision/cancelled-pointerup-still-clicks).

- **F1 A, the founder's ruling — not served now.** Circle Drawer gets an in-process stand boot read by its checks; no
  carrier, count or served list moves; it is served at «Cold-agent bar» (v040-15).

- **F3 A, F4 A, F5 A and the `data-circles` attribute — the escher overseer's word (a delegate), left standing by the
  founder.** The canvas paints each circle's diameter, numbers only, at its centre. A driver click lands at the
  canvas's centre only, a stated limit until `drag` (v040-12). The canvas states `role="group"` named «Drawing area».
  The circle list reaches the widget as one `data-circles` attribute, parsed in `attribute_changed`, malformed text
  read as no circle and never a panic (security-plan ·
  input-validation/decision/custom-widget-initial-attribute-replay: «checking each value stays the widget's own job»).

The circles leave the DOM, and with it the snapshot, tree, graph and lint. They cross only as shot pixels (security-plan ·
threat-model-summary/decision/canvas-content-crosses-as-shot-pixels). No verb, argument, carrier, field, cause, session error,
exit, log field or span is added. Every new check is controlled and its red reading kept (the operator's directive,
`inputs#I1`; test-plan · unit-test-strategy/decision/mutation-controlled-tests).

1. **The engine check first, red.** Create `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_click.rs`. It keeps arch S1–S7,
   tests S1–S7, security S1 and S4, obs S1, design S1–S2 and layouts S2.
   - Its `//!` doc names the behaviour: an app's click and double click on a custom-widget element reach its
     handlers, both layout modes. It also names upstream's behaviour it changes: the widget arm returns before the
     click synthesis (arch S7).
   - A private widget `PointerLog` paints nothing and records each `UiEvent::PointerDown` and `UiEvent::PointerUp` it
     hears into a shared cell (an `Arc<Mutex<Vec<&'static str>>>`), as the P3 probe did
     (`evidence/probe_cd_click.rs.txt`).
   - One component, booted through `stand::boot_alone(…, stand::options(incremental))` inside
     `Session::start("canvas", …)`. It holds an `object` keyed `canvas` (`display: block; width: 200px; height:
     100px;`) carrying a `CustomWidgetAttr` of the widget, an `onclick` and an `ondoubleclick` that count into two
     signals, and a `p` reading `clicks {n} dbl {m}`.
   - Two tests, each in both layout modes:
     - `one_click_on_a_canvas_reaches_the_apps_click_handler`: the fixture's condition first, the snapshot holds the
       `canvas` node. Then one driver `click` is accepted; the app reads `clicks 1 dbl 0`; the widget heard
       `[down, up]`.
     - `two_clicks_with_no_advance_reach_the_apps_double_click_handler`: two `click`s with no `advance` between them
       read `clicks 2 dbl 1`, the widget `[down, up, down, up]`. Then `advance` 600 and a third `click` read
       `clicks 3 dbl 1` (architecture · standard-contracts/decision/double-click-window).
   - Run gate 2 on the untouched engine: red, `clicks 0 dbl 0` with the widget's events heard, as the probe measured.
     Keep the log, every host path respelled, as
     `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas/evidence/red-canvas-click.log`.

2. **The engine change.** In `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs`, add a private escher function
   `widget_click_synthesis(doc, target, data)`, gated `#[cfg(feature = "custom-widget")]`. Its `///` cites the UI
   Events click and dblclick definitions (`https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-click`; arch S7). It does three
   things:
   - On `PointerDown`, `record_pointerdown` at the event's page point, which counts the click on the document's clock.
   - On `PointerUp`, `handle_pointerup(doc, target, event, false)`, which queues the UA `Click` (main button) or
     `ContextMenu` (secondary) as for any element.
   - On `Click`, queue `DoubleClick` to the target when `doc.click_count == 2`. It runs no `click_walk` and no
     `clear_focus`, so the focus the widget arm set stands (research §The F2 A mechanism).
   In `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs`, the widget arm of `handle_dom_event` calls it once, after
   `widget_data.widget.handle_event` and the focus set, before its `return`. That is one call in upstream's body. The
   prevented branch (`:136-140`) and the sub-document arm are untouched. No log site, span or field (obs S3, security
   S4). Gate 2 then reads 2 passed; gates 1 and 9 green.

3. **The sample's widget and markup.** In `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs`:
   - A private widget `CircleCanvas` holds the parsed circles, the handed font context (`Widget::fonts`) and a
     `parley::LayoutContext`.
     - `attribute_changed` reads `data-circles`: `x,y,d` triples, `;`-separated, finite numbers only. A malformed
       triple is skipped, malformed text reads as no circle, and nothing panics.
     - `paint` fills each circle `rgba(58, 92, 229, 0.15)` and strokes it 2 px `#3a5ce5` (layout-templates ·
       surface-desktop-native/decision/stand-accent-colour). It then shapes the diameter as an integer, 12 px
       `sans-serif` in `#1a1a1a`, centred on the circle, and draws its glyph runs as `stand_canvas_cross_os`'s
       `DocumentGlyphs` does. No `expect` or `unwrap`: a poisoned lock is read through
       `unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)`, and no font context handed draws no text.
   - The `div#circle-canvas` and its `div.circle` children become one `object` with `id: "circle-canvas"`, `class:
     "cd-canvas"`, `role: "group"` and `aria-label: "Drawing area"`, attributes alone (layouts S1; layout-templates ·
     surface-desktop-native/decision/stand-a11y-by-attributes-alone).
     - `"data"` carries `use_hook(|| CustomWidgetAttr::new(CircleCanvas::default()))`.
     - `"data-circles"` is rendered from `circles()`. Its writes reach the widget as tracked mutations (research,
       `mutator.rs:330-380`).
     - The `onmounted`, `onclick` and `ondoubleclick` handlers and their graph declarations stay as written.
     - `.cd-canvas` adds `display: block`; the `.circle` rules go.
   - A `#[cfg(test)]` unit test, `malformed_circle_text_reads_as_no_circle`, feeds `attribute_changed` an empty value,
     `"x"`, `"1,2"`, `"1,2,NaN"`, `"1,2,inf"` and `"10,20,40;bad;30,40,50"`, and reads 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 and 2 circles.

4. **The crates.** `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]` gains `anyrender`, `parley` and `peniko`, each
   `{ workspace = true }` (architecture · conventions/decision/workspace-dependencies). They go in the target-free
   table, since the lib also builds for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. The lock's `seven_guis` entry gains its three lines,
   written by one resolution with no `--locked` (`cargo tree --offline -p seven_guis --depth 0`), as the previous
   chunk took `parley`. No package is added (read by gate 10). Every later cargo run passes `--locked`.

5. **The stand boot.** In `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`, add `pub fn boot_circle_drawer(options: HarnessOptions)
   -> Harness<DioxusDocument>` beside `boot_order`. It is `Harness::from_vdom` over a root rendering
   `task_in_shell(Task::CircleDrawer, …)`, offline, and its `///` names it in process only, served by no
   `escher-session` role (F1 A). Add one inline test, `circle_drawer_boots_in_the_shell`, beside
   `the_order_page_boots_in_the_shell`: both layout modes read `#task-title` «Circle Drawer» and `#circle-canvas`
   present.

6. **The sample check.** Create `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_circle_drawer_canvas.rs`, keeping step 1's standing
   lines and a11y S2–S3. Its `//!` names the behaviour. Each test boots `stand::boot_circle_drawer` in a `Session` and
   runs in both layout modes. Shots are read through the driver's `screenshot` with an id and decoded through the
   `png` dev-dependency. Every pixel and count is pinned as the literal the first run measures, never derived (test-plan ·
   unit-test-strategy/decision/expected-value-pinned-as-literal). Four tests:
   - `circle_drawer_boots_with_a_named_keyed_canvas_and_no_lint_finding`:
     - the snapshot's `circle-canvas` reads role `Group`, name «Drawing area», `clickable`;
     - `circle-undo` and `circle-redo` read not enabled;
     - `lint` answers 0 findings;
     - `unkeyed_actionable()` is empty.
   - `a_click_paints_a_circle_and_its_diameter_on_the_canvas`:
     - one `click` on `circle-canvas` is accepted, and the object's `data-circles` holds one circle of diameter 40;
     - the canvas element shot differs from the boot shot;
     - the shot holds the stroke colour on the ring and dark diameter glyphs inside a central label box (a pixel is
       dark when every channel is at most 128). The ring pixels and the dark-pixel count are pinned as measured.
   - `undo_and_redo_repaint_the_canvas`:
     - after the click and `advance` 600, `click circle-undo` gives a canvas shot byte-equal to the boot shot;
     - `click circle-redo` gives one byte-equal to the after-click shot.
   - `two_centre_clicks_open_the_dialog_and_its_slider_resizes_the_circle`:
     - `click`, then `click` again with no `advance`: `circle-diameter` and `circle-close` stand (a double click,
       F4 A);
     - `click circle-diameter` moves the slider, and `data-circles` and the canvas shot change from before it;
     - `click circle-close` removes the dialog.
   - Run gate 4 on the tree as step 3 leaves it, before step 5: it does not build (`stand::boot_circle_drawer` is
     absent). Then, with step 5 in place and step 3's `data-circles` write held back, run it red: the second test's
     shot reads equal to the boot shot. Keep
     `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas/evidence/red-circle-drawer.log`.

7. **The cross-OS row.** In `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_cross_os.rs`:
   - Add a second table `SAMPLE: [Row; 2]`, the Circle Drawer canvas's element shot after one centre click, in both
     layout modes, with its own row count asserted (test-plan · unit-test-strategy/decision/table-tests-count-their-rows).
   - Add one test, `circle_drawers_canvas_reads_its_digest`. It boots `stand::boot_circle_drawer`, sends one `click` on
     `circle-canvas`, then `screenshot` with `circle-canvas`, and holds `answer_digest` equal to `SAMPLE`.
   - The whole screen holds page text and is never shot here (test-plan · test-strategy/decision/no-shot-in-cross-os-byte-checks).
     The `//!` gains one sentence naming the sample's row.
   - The digests are the literals the first linux run measures. CI's linux, windows and macOS legs read them equal or
     the chunk is red (the acceptance).

8. **The moved readings.** In `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_non_lean_tasks.rs`, `circle_drawer_with_dialog` reads the
   canvas's `data-circles` attribute, one circle, in place of `.circle`. `MEASURED` and `CLICKABLE` keep Circle
   Drawer's rows, re-pinned to what gate 6 measures. Predicted 1 → 0 each, since the canvas now states `role="group"`;
   record the measured value against the prediction. The other readers that open Circle Drawer from Home
   (`stand_graph`, `stand_handler_coverage`, `stand_actionable_keys`) and the shared `GRAPH_DRIVES` /
   `UNEXERCISED_AFTER_DRIVES` rows are predicted unchanged: the id, handlers and declarations move with the canvas
   (research §Sweeps). A reading that moves stops the step and is reported, never re-pinned silently.

10. **The controls.** After gates 1–8 read green, /implement makes ONE one-shot `gate.py control` run, never an entry
    (gate-contract.md §Control). Its controls file is in the run dir, with five controls, each `case` its guard's own
    test, each edit's `old` text the line as /implement wrote it:
    - `widget-click` · entry 2 · the `widget_click_synthesis(…)` call in the widget arm removed · case
      `one_click_on_a_canvas_reaches_the_apps_click_handler` (red reading: `clicks 0 dbl 0`, step 1's);
    - `data-circles` · entry 4 · the `"data-circles"` attribute line removed from the object · case
      `a_click_paints_a_circle_and_its_diameter_on_the_canvas` (red reading: the shot equals the boot shot);
    - `diameter-text` · entry 4 · the widget's `draw_glyphs` call removed · case
      `a_click_paints_a_circle_and_its_diameter_on_the_canvas` (red reading: no dark pixel in the label box);
    - `canvas-role` · entry 4 · the object's `role` and `aria-label` lines removed · case
      `circle_drawer_boots_with_a_named_keyed_canvas_and_no_lint_finding` (red reading: role `Unknown`, name empty);
    - `canvas-digest` · entry 5 · the widget's stroke colour `#3a5ce5` changed to `#3a5ce4` · case
      `circle_drawers_canvas_reads_its_digest` (red reading: the digest differs from `SAMPLE`).
    Each entry carries `--no-fail-fast`. Kill `--timeout 1200` (a per-package rebuild of blitz-dom or seven_guis and
    their dependents, plus one target). A `timeout` reading is not read as held: that control is re-fired once, then
    stopped on. The five `holds` lines are recorded beside the red readings of steps 1 and 6. The parse's unit test
    (step 3) is its own control: each malformed input is a case that panics or reads a circle if the parse is made
    infallible.
11. **The wider gates.** Gates 6–14, in order.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_click.rs` — the engine check of an app's click and double click on a canvas (F2 A)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_circle_drawer_canvas.rs` — Circle Drawer's canvas: boot readings, the shot, the flow
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — `widget_click_synthesis`, the escher function (step 2)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs` — its one call in the widget arm of `handle_dom_event` (step 2)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs` — the `CircleCanvas` widget, the `<object>` canvas, the parse's unit test (step 3)
- `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml` — `anyrender`, `parley`, `peniko`, workspace-inherited (step 4)
- `Cargo.lock` — the `seven_guis` entry's three dependency lines; no package added (step 4)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs` — `boot_circle_drawer` and its inline test (step 5)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_cross_os.rs` — `SAMPLE` and `circle_drawers_canvas_reads_its_digest` (step 7)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_non_lean_tasks.rs` — the `data-circles` reading, `MEASURED` and `CLICKABLE` (step 8)
- `docs/capabilities.md` — the canvas sample, its witnesses and the centre-click limit (step 9)
**The gates:**
- blitz-dom's unit tests (gate 1);
- the engine check, red before step 2 (gate 2);
- seven_guis' lib tests: the parse's unit test and the stand's inline boots (gate 3);
- the sample check, red before step 3's carriage (gate 4);
- the cross-OS table with its new row (gate 5);
- the readers that open Circle Drawer or hold a widget, which must read as predicted (gate 6);
- the whole of blitz-tests per package (gate 7);

- seven_guis' package tests, its process checks included, so the binary that now holds the widget still answers
  (gate 8);
- the custom-widget layout reader under the workspace's features (gate 9);
- the lock probe, three lines added, none removed against the commit this chunk starts from (gate 10);

- the pre-push gate `fast` (gate 11), whose workspace tests, both clippy lines and `embolden` read the engine change
  and the widget's glyph paint;
- the `build` leg, which builds seven_guis for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with the widget's crates (gate 12);
- the `audit` leg, since the lock moves (gate 13; security-plan · dependency-security/decision/dependency-audit-cargo-deny);
- `stand-repeat`, which takes both new `stand_` files by their prefix (gate 14).

**What no step changes:** no served task, kept check or committed check (F1 A), so `stand_cross_os_readings`' table,
`host_log`, `mcp_log` and the cold-agent pipe move nothing; all of them are read inside `fast` and `stand-repeat`. No log
site, span or field. No public item or public doc comment: `widget_click_synthesis` is private, so the `doc` leg is not
listed. No a11y leg file: the new checks read role and name through the snapshot, no AccessKit tree test, so they meet
none of the leg's criteria (test-plan · ci-integration/decision/a11y-leg-membership); the leg's file count, which the
capability pin reads, does not move. No boot path of a binary changes, and no served task holds the sample, so there
is no smoke entry. There is no live leg and no headful self-verify on this project.

**Controls.** Each new check reads red before the code it guards (steps 1 and 6), and under step 10's one-shot
`gate.py control`; gate 10 reads `0+0` on the untouched tree. No other new control.

**What CI reads.** The acceptance needs CI's three hosts to read the sample's canvas digest equal (gate 5 inside each
host's test leg). The diff is not OS-sensitive otherwise: no OS `cfg` site is added (the added `cfg` is the
`custom-widget` feature's). The canvas's glyphs are drawn by the widget, and widget glyph runs read byte-equal on the
three hosts (`stand_canvas_cross_os`, «Hg», CI#45209188300). The operator's hygiene, push and CI entries stand.

  Drawer's canvas element shot after one centre click is held to `SAMPLE` in both layout modes, and the CI run the

  `3+0`.

- matrix#v040-09 — on the stand, a shot of Circle Drawer shows the circles its app painted from Rust and canvas text
  drawn from the bundled fonts, in both layout modes (`stand_circle_drawer_canvas`); the canvas shot's bytes are held
  equal on CI's Linux, macOS and Windows hosts by its digest row (`stand_canvas_cross_os` in the CI run above), as
  the founder required (byte equality, F1 of 2026-11-23-canvas-shot-across-hosts).

- Spec anchors: architecture · established-decisions/decision/custom-widget-object, canvas-crosses-as-pixels,
  direct-engine-changes-flagged-upstreamable, harness-paints-custom-widgets; architecture ·
  stack-and-technologies/decision/fork-additions-in-own-functions; architecture ·
  standard-contracts/decision/double-click-window, stand-typography-dejavu-sans, actionable-elements-keyed,
  contract/nodes-widgets/widget-fonts, contract/headless-stand/boot; architecture ·

  input-validation/decision/cancelled-pointerup-still-clicks, custom-widget-initial-attribute-replay,
  event-is-trusted-by-source; security-plan · threat-model-summary/decision/canvas-content-crosses-as-shot-pixels;
  test-plan · test-strategy/decision/canvas-shots-cross-os-by-digest, no-shot-in-cross-os-byte-checks; test-plan ·
  unit-test-strategy/decision/mutation-controlled-tests, expected-value-pinned-as-literal; layout-templates ·
  surface-desktop-native/decision/stand-a11y-by-attributes-alone, stand-lints-clean-at-boot, stand-accent-colour.

- Research files inspected: `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs`,
  `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/driver.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs`,
  `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs`, `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`,
  `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_cross_os.rs`,
  `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_non_lean_tasks.rs`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`, `docs/capabilities.md`.
- The forks: `inputs#I2` (answers), `inputs#I3` (the resume), `evidence/founder-forks.md` (the questions).

- Leaned «a11y leg not joined» per test-plan · ci-integration/decision/a11y-leg-membership: the checks read the
  snapshot, no AccessKit tree test.

- Leaned «no 0.4.0 witness table here» per the working route's «Stand requirement sweep» entry, which owns 0.4.0's
  capabilities proven inside stand-repeat. `git grep -n -E 'WITNESSES_040|v040-' --
  tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_requirement_sweep.rs` reads 0 hits.

- Running `handle_click` for a widget target — rejected: `click_walk` matches no arm for an `<object>` and
  `handle_click` then clears focus, undoing the widget arm's focus (research §The F2 A mechanism).
- A DOM hit layer over the canvas (F2 B) or widget-owned input (F2 C) — not taken, the founder's F2 A.
- An offset argument on `click` (F4 B) — not taken; the verb table and its seven argument kinds stay as they are.
- Serving Circle Drawer from `escher-session` (F1 B) — not taken; no served list, count or cold-agent app moves.
- A circle as a DOM node or a virtual node — no: circles cross as pixels alone until v040-11.
- A screenshot of Circle Drawer's whole screen in a cross-OS byte check — no: it holds page text.
- `expect` or `unwrap` in the sample's widget — no: a poisoned lock and malformed text are read, never panicked on.

- The engine function sits in `pointer.rs` beside `record_pointerdown` and `handle_pointerup`, which it calls. Its one
  call in `events/mod.rs` moves cited lines; the wrap re-points the citations.

- The synthesized `Click` and `DoubleClick` are queued through `queue_ua_event`, so they read `isTrusted` true
  (security-plan · input-validation/decision/event-is-trusted-by-source) and pass the app's listener chain, the
  signal registry's dispatch and the reached record as any click does.

- `handle_click` is held below the cognitive-complexity ceiling (test-plan ·
  quality-gates-coverage-targets/decision/complexity-ceiling-host-only) and is not touched.

- The sample's `onclick` reads the canvas origin through `MountedData::get_client_rect` on the `<object>`; the click
  lands at its centre, so the first circle reads `350,200,40` against the 700 × 400 box. That is a prediction, measured
  by gate 4.

- The CARRY `cry-p6543j6z` (the «24 `stand_*` readers» leaf count in `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`) is the
  wrap's whole-mode leaf pass; no implement step. This chunk adds two `stand_` files, neither declaring `mod fixtures;`.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Established Decisions — a row for the click synthesis on a custom-widget
  target, ratified, a direct engine change flagged upstreamable, guard `stand_canvas_click`; the founder's F2
  «A: движок создаёт click (Recommended)», relayed verbatim (`inputs#I2`). The tally of direct engine changes
  (architecture · established-decisions/decision/direct-engine-changes-flagged-upstreamable) names it.

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Input Validation — the same engine change for every document behind
  `custom-widget`, with no carrier, verb, field, cause, log field or span added; the founder's F2 word as above. It
  meets the playbook's boundary-widening pattern (`rul-izni57qv`) only in so far as it changes engine behaviour for
  every document. That call is the founder's, and he answered it himself.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts — `contract/headless-stand/boot` gains Circle Drawer's
  in-process boot, served by no role (F1 A, the founder's ruling).

- Expected amendments (wrap): layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native — `decision/stand-lints-clean-at-boot` gains
  Circle Drawer; `contract/stand-element-ids/circle-canvas` states the canvas `<object>`, `role="group"` named
  «Drawing area». F5 A is the escher overseer's word (a delegate), left standing by the founder (`inputs#I2`).

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §2 Test Strategy — `decision/canvas-shots-cross-os-by-digest` gains Circle
  Drawer's canvas element shot.
- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §6 Log Coverage — the two new checks silent, no log site added.

2. **The engine change.** In `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs`, add a private escher function
   `widget_click_synthesis(doc, target, data)`, gated `#[cfg(feature = "custom-widget")]`. Its `///` cites the UI
   Events click and dblclick definitions (`https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-click`; arch S7). It does three
   things:
   - On `PointerDown`, `record_pointerdown` at the event's page point, which counts the click on the document's clock.
   - On `PointerUp`, `handle_pointerup(doc, target, event, false)`, which queues the UA `Click` (main button) or
     `ContextMenu` (secondary) as for any element.
   - On `Click`, queue `DoubleClick` to the target when `doc.click_count == 2`. It runs no `click_walk` and no
     `clear_focus`, so the focus the widget arm set stands (research §The F2 A mechanism).
   In `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs`, the widget arm of `handle_dom_event` calls it once, after

record.title: A canvas painted headless
record.requirement: What an app paints into a canvas from Rust appears in a headless screenshot, its text from the bundled fonts, its cross-host byte equality measured and required or given a tolerance by the founder's word; Circle Drawer moves onto a real canvas
record.observed_gap: An app paints through the widget trait, appended behind a feature the headless harness drops unless another crate unifies it, so whether a headless shot paints a widget at all is unmeasured; the CPU backend paints custom and resource paints transparent with no warning; a widget's paint gets the border-box size placed at the content-box origin (upstream #1578); no stand app holds a canvas, Circle Drawer's canvas being an ordinary element.

verification.acceptance: On the stand, Circle Drawer's canvas element shot after one centre click holds the circle ring and its diameter glyphs, painted by the app's widget from Rust with text shaped from the document's own font context (the bundled DejaVu Sans), in both layout modes (`stand_circle_drawer_canvas`); its answer digest is held byte-equal to one committed `SAMPLE` table in both layout modes by `stand_canvas_cross_os`, read green on CI's linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 test legs in the run the operator's `ci.py` entry reads (byte equality, the founder's F1 of 2026-11-23-canvas-shot-across-hosts); the whole screen holds page text and stays outside every cross-OS byte check.

record.notes:
2026-11-23 (2026-11-23-canvas-in-a-headless-shot, phase P5): not claimed — a widget painted from Rust on an `<object data>` is planned to show in a harness and a driver shot in every build selection, on the stand in process (stand_canvas_shot); the acceptance's Circle Drawer, canvas text and cross-host legs stay with «Canvas placement and text», «Canvas shot across hosts» and «Circle Drawer on a canvas».

2026-11-23 (2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text, phase P5): not claimed — a widget's paint placed at its content box inside its element's transform (upstream #1578), its pointer events in the same content-box frame, and canvas text shaped from the document's own font context are planned on the stand in process (stand_canvas_placement, stand_canvas_pointer_frame, stand_canvas_text), on the founder's F1 A+C and F2 A; the acceptance's Circle Drawer and cross-host legs stay with «Canvas shot across hosts» and «Circle Drawer on a canvas».

2026-11-23 (2026-11-23-canvas-shot-across-hosts, phase P5): not claimed — the acceptance's cross-host leg is planned on canvas-only stand fixtures (a fill, an antialiased edge, canvas glyphs; whole and element shots, both layout modes) held byte-equal to one committed digest table on CI's linux x86_64, macOS aarch64 and windows x86_64 (stand_canvas_cross_os), on the founder's F1 A «A: требовать побайтовое равенство (Recommended)» (relayed verbatim); the acceptance's Circle Drawer shot stays with «Circle Drawer on a canvas», whose element shot of its canvas joins the same table.

2026-11-23 (2026-11-23-canvas-shot-across-hosts, wrap P7.3): the cross-host part, held unclaimed — three canvas-only fixtures (a solid fill, an antialiased edge, canvas glyphs), whole and element shots in both layout modes, read byte-equal by their answer digests on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 against one committed table, no pixels committed (`stand_canvas_cross_os`, CI#45209188300 on `0ebf3c5ef`, 17/17 green, `5 passed` on each host). Byte equality is REQUIRED of a canvas-only shot, on the founder's F1 «A: требовать побайтовое равенство (Recommended)» (2026-11-23, relayed verbatim by overseer1 and the escher overseer); a shot holding page text stays out of every cross-OS byte check. The capability stays pooled for «Circle Drawer on a canvas», whose canvas element shot joins the same table (the operator's P5 direction, route WATCH). Unmeasured: a CPU without AVX2, a scale other than 1.0, gradients, images, clips, blends, larger glyph sets. Authority for leaving it unclaimed: the operator's wrap directive, point 4.

body:
**Chunk:** Circle Drawer on a canvas — the stand sample's circles and canvas text painted from Rust, keyed, boot lint clean, checked in both layout modes, its canvas shot in the cross-OS digest table
**Date:** 2026-11-23
**Run:** 2026-11-23T21-22-31-implement

- **Files:** new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_click.rs`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_circle_drawer_canvas.rs`;
  modified `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs`,
  `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs`, `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`,
  `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_canvas_cross_os.rs`,
  `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_non_lean_tasks.rs`, `docs/capabilities.md` (basis: `cites.py added`,
  `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-23T21-22-31-implement/new-text.md`: 11 files, 2 new).

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - blitz-dom: `widget_click_synthesis(doc, target, data)`, `pub(crate)`, `#[cfg(feature = "custom-widget")]`
    (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` 817-835, per new-text.md) — on a custom-widget target, after the
    widget's `handle_event` and the focus set: a `PointerDown` runs `record_pointerdown`, a `PointerUp` runs
    `handle_pointerup(…, false)` (UA `Click` on the main button, `ContextMenu` on the secondary), a `Click` with
    `click_count == 2` queues `DoubleClick`; no `click_walk`, no `clear_focus`. One call in upstream's
    `handle_dom_event` widget arm (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs`, 2 added lines). No public item. An engine
    change for every document behind `custom-widget` (every Dioxus native app): an app's `onclick` and
    `ondoubleclick` on a widget element now fire, the widget still hearing every pointer event first; upstream's
    arm returned before the synthesis. Flagged upstreamable, nothing sent.
  - seven_guis: `pub fn stand::boot_circle_drawer(options: HarnessOptions) -> Harness<DioxusDocument>`
    (`examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs` 268-272) — in process only, served by no `escher-session` role; the module
    doc names Circle Drawer among the stand's boots.
  - seven_guis Circle Drawer (private): `CircleCanvas` (a `Widget`: `attribute_changed` reads `data-circles`,
    `fonts` keeps the handed context, `paint` fills each circle `rgba(58, 92, 229, 38/255)`, strokes it 2 px `#3a5ce5`
    inside its edge, draws the diameter as an integer, 12 px `sans-serif`, `#1a1a1a`, centred, the scene clipped to
    the paint box), `parse_circles`, `circles_text`, `Painted`, `CANVAS_BORDER` (2 px). `div#circle-canvas` and its
    `div.circle` children are now one `object#circle-canvas.cd-canvas`, `role="group"`, `aria-label` «Drawing area»,
    `"data"` a `CustomWidgetAttr`, `"data-circles"` rendered from the circles (`x,y,d` per circle, `;`-joined);
    `onclick` / `ondoubleclick` read the point against the canvas's content box (border subtracted).
  - No verb, argument, carrier, field, cause, session error, exit, log field or span added; circles leave the DOM,
    snapshot, tree, graph and lint and cross as shot pixels alone.
- **Crates / modules:** none added or removed; blitz-dom's events and the seven_guis lib changed.

- **Dependencies:** seven_guis `[dependencies]` (target-free) gains `anyrender`, `blitz-dom`, `parley`, `peniko`, each
  `{ workspace = true }`; `Cargo.lock`'s `seven_guis` entry gains those four lines, no package added
  (`git diff -- Cargo.lock`: 4 added, 0 removed).

- **Schema / config:** none — `data-circles` is an attribute inside the sample, parsed by its widget, malformed text
  read as no circle.
- **Spec-master edits:** none.
- **Retired:** the `.circle` DOM nodes and their CSS rules in Circle Drawer (no census row).

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:**
  - `stand_non_lean_tasks` `MEASURED` and `CLICKABLE`: Circle Drawer 1 → 0 each (the canvas states `role="group"`).
  - `stand_canvas_cross_os`: 5 → 6 tests, a second table `SAMPLE` of 2 rows beside `TABLE`'s 12.
  - `docs/capabilities.md`: the canvas claim gains Circle Drawer and the click on a widget element; Witnesses
    `stand_circle_drawer_canvas`, `stand_canvas_click`; one stated limit added («A click lands at an element's
    centre»); the proven section names both checks. No pinned count moved (gate `fast`'s capability pin green).
  - `stand_` files: two added (`stand_canvas_click`, `stand_circle_drawer_canvas`), neither declaring `mod fixtures;`,
    both declaring `mod session_common;`.
- **Dev-tool versions:** none.
- **Harness / gate surface:** none.

- **Cross-project / external claims:** `inputs#I1` (the operator's direction), `inputs#I2` (the forks' answers as
  relayed: F1 A, F2 A the founder's; F3 A, F4 A, F5 A and `data-circles` the escher overseer's word, left standing),
  `inputs#I3` (the operator's resume at P4). No CI run read by this run.
- **Reverted / negative API facts:** none.
- **Insufficient fixes (written, kept, not the remedy):** none.

- **Spec claims disproved by measurement:**
  - The plan's step 4 and gate 9: «three lock lines» (`anyrender`, `parley`, `peniko`) — measured four: `Widget::paint`
    names `blitz_dom::node::ComputedStyles`, which no crate seven_guis depends on re-exports, so `blitz-dom` is a
    fourth dependency (gate 9 `last line 4+0`).
  - The plan's implementation note: «the first circle reads `350,200,40` against the 700 × 400 box» — measured
    `348,198,40`: the canvas is a 700 × 400 border box, its content box 696 × 396, and the app now reads the click
    against the content box (`stand_circle_drawer_canvas`).

- **Expected amendments (from plan):**
  - architecture §Established Decisions — the click synthesis on a custom-widget target, ratified (F2), guard

title: evidence/founder-forks.md
body:
# Operator forks — 2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas («Circle Drawer on a canvas», v040-09)

Written at phase P4 on the operator's direction (`inputs#I1`): every fork that is the operator's — a boundary widening,
a new served task or carrier, a new verb, crossing or public surface, a choice that turns what the sample or the
canvas is — is listed here unanswered. No plan is written until these are answered. A recommendation is marked
where one artifact supports it. It is a lean, not an answer.

Measured basis (`evidence/probe-cd-click.log`, a scratch-worktree probe at HEAD `a199c213e`, both layout modes):
- An app's `onclick` and `ondoubleclick` on a canvas `<object>` NEVER fire. Two driver clicks are accepted, and the
  widget hears down and up twice. The app reads 0 clicks and 0 double clicks. A pointer event on a custom-widget target
  is forwarded to `Widget::handle_event` and returns before `handle_pointerup` queues `Click` and `DoubleClick`
  (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs:183-207`, `events/pointer.rs:744,791,813`).
- A canvas `<object>` reads role `Unknown`, `clickable: true`, no name, and takes focus on a pointer press
  (`events/mod.rs:200-202`). It reads 0 lint findings and `unkeyed_actionable` 0.
- Today's Circle Drawer reads 0 lint findings and `unkeyed_actionable` 0 at boot.
- A driver `click` lands at the element's centre. Two clicks with no `advance` between them read as a double click.

Playbook pattern met by the forks marked so: `rul-izni57qv` — **Boundary widening** (always a human's call, never a
routine rule; the wrap halts on it once, as the answer card, when the operator's own word answers it; a delegate's
answer leaves it the wrap's full escalation).

---

## F1 — Is Circle Drawer a served task of `escher-session`?

**What crosses:** if served, Circle Drawer's screen goes onto every ratified carrier: the session socket, the command
line, MCP, kept checks and the coverage role. That screen is ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs, the graph,
actions, layout answers, lint findings, and the canvas as shot pixels. Once it joins the cold-agent app set it also
reaches the model provider on a live run. The content classes are all ratified, the canvas pixels included
(`decision/canvas-crosses-as-pixels`, on every carrier, the provider included). A new app on the closed `TASKS`
table adds no carrier (security precedent `amd-qr32fehm`). But the last served addition, the order page, had its
crossing to the provider widened by the founder (`amd-quedt6kc`).

**Rule:** `rul-izni57qv` (boundary widening) for the provider leg, if the cold-agent app set takes it. Without that,
the operator's own direction (a new served task).

**Options:**
- **A — Stay in process now (recommended).** Circle Drawer gets a stand boot (`stand::boot_circle_drawer`, like
  `boot_order`), read by its in-process checks. No carrier, count or served list moves. It is served at «Cold-agent
  bar» (v040-15), which already widens the pipe to canvas apps. Cost: 1 function in `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`,
  0 served-list sites.
- **B — Serve it now** (slug `circle-drawer`, the eighth). Measured cost:
  - The served-list sites: `git grep -n -E '"order"'` reads 40 hits in 15 files — `session_host.rs`,
    `cli_commands.rs`, `host_log.rs`, `common/mod.rs`, `session_common/mod.rs`, `stand_actions.rs`,
    `stand_cross_os_readings.rs`, `stand_explore.rs`, `stand_graph.rs`, `stand_handler_coverage.rs`, `stand_layout.rs`,
    `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py`, `scripts/cold-agent.sh`, and more.
  - The count phrases (`seven served|…`): 30 hits, among them `docs/capabilities.md` ×5 and its pin, `CLAUDE.md` and
    11 `.claude/docs` leaves.
  - New `stand_cross_os_readings` rows (boot and step × snapshot parts · lint · actions × 2 modes), read on linux here
    and proven on windows and macOS only by the next CI run.
  - Moved master rows at the wrap: `contract/escher-session-cli/usage`, `contract/escher-session/invocation`,
    `decision/stand-readings-same-on-every-ci-os`, `decision/cross-os-readings-by-answer-digest`,
    `contract/escher-session-command-line/start`, and the cold-agent rows.

**Dependences:**
- B adds about 15 files and a count sweep, and the entry then SPLITS (sizing below).
- With A, v040-15 owns the serving and its sweep.
- v040-10's «same answer … on every CI host» reads in process under either option.

---

## F2 — How does a click reach the sample, now that an app's click handlers on a canvas never fire?

**What crosses:** nothing new on any driver carrier under any option. What changes is engine behaviour (A), or what the
canvas is (B, C).

**Rule:**
- A is a behaviour change for every document behind `custom-widget`. `dioxus-native` turns that feature on, so it
  reaches every Dioxus native app. A behaviour change for every document with no ruling behind it is the founder's
  (session learning 2026-10-18), and escher's addition sits in a function of its own
  (`decision/fork-additions-in-own-functions`).
- B and C turn what the canvas is.

**Options:**
- **A — Engine: a pointer press and release on a canvas still make a click (recommended).** After forwarding the
  event to the widget, the engine still runs the pointer-up's click and double-click synthesis for a custom-widget
  target, so the app's `onclick` and `ondoubleclick` on the `<object>` fire. The widget still hears every event, and
  this is upstreamable.
  - Cost: one function in `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs`, and one new engine check in both modes. The sample
    keeps its handlers, its `circle-canvas` id (on the object), its graph declarations and `GRAPH_DRIVES`.
  - The scope gains an engine file, so the row read over the masters it reaches runs again (about 15 min).
  - Its new control: the check reads `clicks 1 dbl 0` after one driver click and `dbl 1` after two. Red reading: the
    forward-and-return restored reads `clicks 0 dbl 0`, as the probe measured.
- **B — A DOM hit layer.** `div#circle-canvas` keeps its handlers and holds the `<object>` at `pointer-events: none`;
  the widget only paints.
  - Cost: `circle_drawer.rs` alone, with the `CLICKABLE` and `MEASURED` pins unchanged.
  - Dependence: v040-11 («a click on one acts on its circle», refused `covered` …) then hit-tests a canvas that takes
    no pointer, so every circle's point lands on the div. A virtual node's covered check would read its own div over
    it, and that design meets this at v040-11.
- **C — Input owned by the widget.** The widget reads pointer down and up itself and hands the point to the app over
  a channel that a Dioxus task drains. Cost:
  - The circle writes come from a task, so the graph reads them undeclared (a stated limit).
  - Double-click detection is re-made inside the widget, which holds no document clock, so a deterministic double
    click is unmeasured.
  - The handler coverage of the canvas is already uncounted.

  This is the highest cost and the entry splits.

**Dependences:** F4 and F5 read differently under B. F3 is independent.

---

## F3 — What canvas text does the sample paint?

**What crosses:** canvas text leaves only as shot pixels (`decision/canvas-crosses-as-pixels`, ratified on every
carrier), so no option widens anything now. At v040-10 the draw-command verb answers the canvas's commands, and its
crossing is that entry's founder fork. What text the canvas holds sets what that verb will carry: numbers, or
authored text.

**Rule:** what the sample is (the operator's direction).

**Options:**
- **A — Each circle's diameter at its centre (recommended).** Numbers only, one label per circle. This is the shape
  v040-10's «a label overflowing its region» and v040-11's per-circle node meet. At boot (no circles) the canvas holds
  no text, so the shot read against matrix#v040-09 is taken after one click.
- **B — A status line inside the canvas** («Click to add a circle» while empty, then «N circles»). This is authored
  text, which v040-10's dump would carry as text.
- **C — Both.**

**Dependences:**
- The cross-OS row (the WATCH) holds the glyphs either way. A canvas holding glyphs was measured byte-equal on the
  three hosts («Hg», `stand_canvas_cross_os`).
- A macOS embolden band pins canvas glyph pixels in the shot check, never in the digest table, where the founder
  requires byte equality.

---

## F4 — Can a driver click place a circle anywhere but the canvas's centre?

**What crosses:** under B, a new argument on a ratified verb, on the socket, the command line, MCP and kept checks.

**Rule:** `rul-izni57qv` (a validated surface admits a new input class). It is also the closed verb schema
(`decision/closed-driver-verb-schema`: seven argument kinds, a fixed refusal order).

**Options:**
- **A — A stated limit until `drag` (recommended).** Every driver-placed circle lands at the canvas's centre. A second
  centre click within the double-click window is a double click and opens the resize dialog. «The drag verb»
  (v040-12) brings «element, virtual node or offset». Cost: a stated limit in `docs/capabilities.md` and the plan.
- **B — An optional offset on `click` now.** Cost: about 10 escher-driver files (`schema`, `command`, `execute`, `cli`,
  `mcp`, `json`, `describe` and their tests), the capability statement's counts and their pin, and a wrap halt. The
  entry splits.

**Dependences:**
- Under F2 B, an offset still lands on the hit layer.
- v040-12 then either reuses or supersedes B's argument.

---

## F5 — What does the canvas state of itself before virtual nodes?

**What crosses:** an author's `aria-label` crosses as a node's name inside the ratified name crossing, so no option
widens anything. What changes is how the canvas reads in the snapshot and the accessibility tree.

**Rule:** what the canvas is (the operator's direction). The a11y-plan's name-and-role reading applies (SC 4.1.2).

**Options:**
- **A — `role="group"` with a name such as «Drawing area» (recommended).** The node names itself and can parent the
  virtual nodes of v040-11. Cost: one attribute pair, and the snapshot pins of the canvas node.
- **B — `role="img"` with a name.** The canvas reads as a picture. Dependence: an `img` role's children are
  presentational, which conflicts with v040-11's per-circle nodes under it.
- **C — Leave it `Unknown` and unnamed** until v040-11, as a stated limit. A focused node with no role and no name
  stands on the sample in the meantime.

**Dependences:** under F2 B the object takes no pointer and no focus, which changes what A–C read.

---

## Technical (asked as a dialog, not here)
- How circle state reaches the widget: one attribute carrying the circle list, or shared state plus a generation
  attribute. Either way an attribute write is the tracked mutation that repaints a window
  (`packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:330-380`). **Answered by the operator (dialog, 2026-11-23): «One attribute
  (Recommended)»** — a `data-circles` attribute on the `<object>`, parsed by the widget in `attribute_changed`, with no
  panic on malformed text.

change taken); `scroll_into_view` scrolls every scrolling box that holds its target, innermost first, skipping a box whose scroll min and max are both zero, then the viewport — a nested box at once by the founder, 2026-10-18), and `get_client_bounding_rect` keeping, for a node a restyle turned display none, the client rect it was last laid out at, and `visible_region` reads each clipping box `aria-label`, `<label>` association (its `for`-target labelable element by id, else its first nested labelable element — HTML's labelable elements, `button`, an `input` whose `type` is not `hidden`, `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select` and `textarea`, matched by the private `is_labelable` — pushed onto the bound element's `labelled_by`), a select's option's non-empty `label` attribute where it engine change for every document, ratified by the founder and flagged upstreamable; check `accessibility_states`; the tree's `focus` is written only where `focus_node_id` is among the built nodes,
